landing.title: Free, open-source SQL editor & database client
landing.description: Free, open-source SQL editor and database client for macOS, Windows and Linux. PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, ClickHouse, DuckDB and lakehouses.
landing.hero.eyebrow: Open source · Made in Germany · No tracking
landing.hero.title: Free SQL editor and
landing.hero.lead: Write SQL. Watch it come alive. A lightweight database GUI for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite, ClickHouse and DuckDB on macOS, Windows and Linux.
landing.video.label: Colwerk launch video
landing.video.description: A short introduction to Colwerk, a lightweight SQL editor and database client for the desktop.
landing.glance.title: What is
landing.glance.summary: Colwerk is a free, open-source (MIT) SQL editor and database client for macOS, Windows and Linux: one desktop GUI for PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, SQL Server, ClickHouse, DuckDB and SQLite that also queries lakehouses and CSV, Parquet, JSON and Excel files with SQL. A built-in MCP server lets AI assistants like Claude, Codex or Cursor explore databases read-only. It runs entirely on your computer: no account, no telemetry, no cloud service.
landing.glance.fact1.label: Price and license
landing.glance.fact1.value: Free and open source under the MIT license. No paid tier, no account, no trial.
landing.glance.fact2.label: Platforms
landing.glance.fact2.value: macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows (x64), Linux (x64 and arm64, .deb). Signed automatic updates on macOS and Windows.
landing.glance.fact3.label: Databases
landing.glance.fact3.value: PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, SQL Server, DuckDB, SQLite, ClickHouse.
landing.glance.fact4.label: Lakehouses and files
landing.glance.fact4.value: Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, Databricks Unity Catalog and Microsoft Fabric OneLake through DuckDB; CSV, TSV, Parquet, JSON and Excel files on disk, S3, Google Cloud Storage or the web.
landing.glance.fact5.label: AI assistants
landing.glance.fact5.value: No built-in AI. A built-in MCP server lets Claude, Codex, Cursor, VS Code or any other MCP client browse schemas and run read-only queries; the assistant hands its final query to a new tab and you decide what runs.
landing.glance.fact6.label: Privacy
landing.glance.fact6.value: No telemetry, no analytics, no account. Passwords are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, with the key in the OS keychain, and are never shown to an AI assistant.
landing.glance.fact7.label: Data tools
landing.glance.fact7.value: Result grid with sorting, filters and row editing; export to CSV, Parquet, Excel, JSON, NDJSON, Markdown and SQL INSERT; data import; schema and data compare; ER diagrams; execution plans; session monitor; masking of personal data.
landing.glance.fact8.label: Switching from another tool
landing.glance.fact8.value: Imports connections from DBeaver, Beekeeper Studio, Azure Data Studio, .pgpass and dbt profiles.yml.
landing.glance.fact9.label: Made by
landing.glance.fact9.value: Dennis Hendricks, Germany. Source code on GitHub.
landing.glance.fit1: Developers and analysts who query PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQL Server every day
landing.glance.fit2: SQL Server users who need a replacement for the retired Azure Data Studio
landing.glance.fit3: Data teams who look into DuckDB files, Parquet, Iceberg or Delta Lake
landing.glance.fit4: Teams with sensitive data: no telemetry, local passwords, masked personal data
landing.glance.fit5: Anyone who wants Claude, Codex or Cursor to explore a database read-only
landing.glance.notFitsTitle: Not the right tool if you need
landing.glance.notFit1: Oracle, MongoDB or other databases beyond the six engines
landing.glance.notFit2: Intel Macs (Colwerk needs Apple Silicon) or Linux distributions without .deb packages
landing.glance.notFit3: A visual query builder: in Colwerk, you write SQL
landing.features.title: A SQL IDE for people who
landing.features.spec1.title: One session per tab
landing.features.spec1.text: Every editor tab holds its own connection. Transactions, temp tables and SET options stay where you left them. If a transaction is still open, Colwerk offers to commit or roll it back.
landing.features.spec2.title: Gentle on your database
landing.features.spec2.text: Drivers read only up to the row limit and cancel the rest. The schema tree loads on demand through its own metadata session, and table sizes come from statistics instead of COUNT(*).
landing.features.spec3.title: Guard rails for production
landing.features.spec3.text: Give a connection a color, for example red for production, and it marks the sidebar, tabs and toolbar. On request, Colwerk asks before any statement that may change data or structures.
landing.features.spec4.title: CSV & Parquet export
landing.features.spec4.text: Export the rows you see or the full result without limit. Colwerk writes the file to disk itself, so large exports never pass through the UI.
landing.features.spec5.title: Built-in MCP server
landing.features.spec5.text: Your AI assistant can browse schemas, run read-only queries and open SQL in a new tab. You decide what actually runs.
landing.features.spec6.title: Local by design
landing.features.spec6.text: Bound to 127.0.0.1 on a random port with a per-start token. Passwords are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and the key lives in your OS keychain.
landing.features.card1.title: A result grid that keeps up
landing.features.card1.text: Sort, filter, pin, hide and resize columns. Search the result, open long values, or copy a row as JSON or CSV.
landing.features.card2.title: Keys in the schema tree
landing.features.card2.text: Primary keys, foreign keys with their target and indexes show right in the tree. Double-click a table to query all its columns.
landing.features.card3.title: Keyboard first
landing.features.card3.text: Format SQL with <kbd>⌘/Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>Shift</kbd> <kbd>F</kbd>, run with <kbd>⌘/Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>Enter</kbd> and open the execution plan with <kbd>⌘/Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>E</kbd>. Multiple cursors and block selection included. Press <kbd>?</kbd> for all shortcuts.
landing.features.card4.title: Sensible defaults
landing.features.card4.text: New tabs start with a limit of 200 rows and a 60-second timeout. Enough to see your data, too little to strain the server. Both can be changed per tab.
landing.features.card5.title: SQL from the schema
landing.features.card5.text: Generate SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE templates with the right parameter style for each engine. UPDATE and DELETE match on the primary key.
landing.features.card6.title: Autocomplete and history
landing.features.card6.text: Autocompletion knows your tables and columns. The last 50 queries are searchable and open in a new tab with one click.
landing.features.card7.title: Opens your files
landing.features.card7.text: Double-click a .sql file to open it in a new tab, or a .duckdb, .sqlite or .sqlite3 file to open it as a connection. If Colwerk is already running, its window comes to the front.
landing.features.card8.title: Tabs in their own window
landing.features.card8.text: Move a tab to a new window and back to the main window when you are done. Each window has its own menu.
landing.privacy.title: Your databases.
landing.privacy.lead: A database client sees everything you query. Colwerk keeps all of it on your machine.
landing.privacy.point1.title: Developed in Germany
landing.privacy.point1.text: Colwerk is built and maintained in Germany. The code is MIT licensed, so anyone can audit it. Updates are signed, and every release includes a software bill of materials.
landing.privacy.point2.title: No tracking
landing.privacy.point2.text: Colwerk has no telemetry, no analytics and no account, and it does not report what you do or which databases you connect to.
landing.privacy.point3.title: No built-in AI
landing.privacy.point3.text: Colwerk sends nothing to any AI service. If you want an assistant, you connect your own and decide which model sees your data.
landing.privacy.point4.title: Credentials stay local
landing.privacy.point4.text: Passwords are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and the key lives in your OS keychain. They never leave your machine and are never shown to an AI.
landing.ai.eyebrow: Bring your own AI. You run it.
landing.ai.title: A database client with a built-in
landing.ai.lead: Colwerk has no AI inside. It speaks MCP, the open Model Context Protocol, so you can connect the cloud or local assistant you already use and decide what it sees. Set it up in one step, or start with example prompts.
landing.ai.step1.title: Ask
landing.ai.step1.text: “Which city buys the most coffee?” in Claude, Codex, Cursor or any other MCP client.
landing.ai.step2.title: Explore
landing.ai.step2.text: Your AI looks at schemas, tables and sample rows and runs read-only queries to find the answer.
landing.ai.step3.title: Hand over
landing.ai.step3.text: The final query opens in a new Colwerk tab, with an explanation as SQL comment.
landing.ai.step4.title: You run it
landing.ai.step4.text: Review it, change it, run it. Colwerk never runs it for you.
landing.ai.can1: Browse connections, schemas, tables and columns
landing.ai.can2: Look at sample rows to understand the data
landing.ai.can3: Run SELECT queries for exploratory analysis
landing.ai.can4: Open finished queries in a new editor tab
landing.ai.cannot2: Insert, update, delete or change the schema
landing.ai.cannot3: Run anything in your editor tabs
landing.ai.cannot4: Connect without its own access token
landing.ai.comment:
-- Which city buys the most coffee?
-- Sums coffee orders per customer city
-- and returns the city with the most cups.
landing.ai.caption: Handed over by your AI, waiting in a new tab for you to run.
landing.ai.note: Queries from your AI run in a separate session inside a read-only transaction that is always rolled back, with a 30 s timeout and a row limit. Setup is a single entry in your MCP client; Colwerk shows it for you. Every call ends up in the audit log, and personal data is masked.
landing.faq.title: Questions,
landing.faq.a1: Yes. Colwerk is open source under the MIT license. There is no paid tier, no account and no trial. The source code is on GitHub for anyone to read and audit.
landing.faq.a2: SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, SQL Server, ClickHouse and DuckDB. Through DuckDB, Colwerk also reads lakehouses: Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, Databricks Unity Catalog and Microsoft Fabric OneLake.
landing.faq.a3: macOS on Apple Silicon, Windows on x64 and Linux on x64 and arm64 as a .deb package. On macOS and Windows, Colwerk installs signed updates itself.
landing.faq.a4: No. There is no telemetry, no analytics and no account. Queries go directly from your computer to your databases. Colwerk only contacts GitHub to check for updates, and DuckDB's extension repository to install the extensions a feature needs.
landing.faq.a5: On your computer only. Passwords are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and the key lives in your operating system’s keychain. They are never shown to an AI assistant.
landing.faq.a6: No. Colwerk has a built-in MCP server instead, so you can connect Claude, Codex, Cursor or any other MCP client you already use. Your AI can explore schemas and run read-only queries, and hands its final query to a new tab. You decide what runs.
landing.faq.q7: Can I use Colwerk with my production database?
landing.faq.a7: Yes, with guard rails. Give the connection a color, for example red, and it marks the sidebar, tabs and toolbar. On request, Colwerk asks before any statement that may change data or structures. New tabs start with a 200-row limit and a 60-second timeout.
landing.faq.q8: Can I use Colwerk as a SQL Server client on a Mac?
landing.faq.a8: Yes. Colwerk runs natively on Macs with Apple Silicon and connects to SQL Server in Docker, on the network or in Azure, with graphical execution plans. It also imports connections from Azure Data Studio, which Microsoft retired in February 2026.
landing.faq.q9: Can I open Parquet, CSV or Excel files without a database?
landing.faq.a9: Yes. Drop the files onto the Colwerk window: each one becomes a view in an in-memory DuckDB database that you query and join with SQL. Files on S3, Google Cloud Storage or the web work too.
landing.faq.q10: How do I switch from DBeaver or another database tool?
landing.faq.a10: Colwerk imports connections from DBeaver, Beekeeper Studio, Azure Data Studio, .pgpass files and dbt profiles.yml, including saved passwords where the other tool stores them readably.
landing.download.title: Download
landing.download.lead: Free, with builds for macOS, Windows and Linux. On macOS and Windows, Colwerk installs signed updates itself.
